rules.title: Preventing Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market (§ 218-12, as amended by Ord. 25-076)
rules.requirement:
Real estate lessors, their agents and their subcontractors may not subscribe to, contract with, exchange anything of value for, or otherwise use the services of a Service Provider. The words "or otherwise utilize" were added by Ord. 25-076.

A Service Provider is any person that performs a coordination function for a real estate lessor. Coordination means three steps:
- collecting nonpublic competitor information from real estate lessors, together with historical or contemporaneous prices, price changes, supply levels, occupancy rates, or lease termination and renewal dates from two or more lessors or from public databases;
- analyzing or processing that information with a system, software or process that uses computation;
- recommending rental prices, lease terms or occupancy levels to a lessor.

Nonpublic competitor information is information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost.

No service provider may facilitate an agreement not to compete among real estate lessors on any aspect of residential dwelling units, including rental pricing, fees or other rental terms.

Enforcement:
- The Attorney General or any municipal or county attorney may sue as parens patriae.
- The Office of Landlord-Tenant Affairs and the Office of Code Compliance enforce the section. Complaints go to the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations, which may refer them for prosecution.
- Any injured person has a private right of action.

A first violation is punishable under Jersey City Code § 1-25. Subsequent violations carry fines of $100 to $2,000, and each day of violation is a separate violation. Successful plaintiffs, including public enforcers, recover costs and reasonable attorney fees.
rules.key_value: First violation per Jersey City Code § 1-25; subsequent violations $100–$2,000; each day a separate violation; costs and reasonable attorney fees to successful plaintiffs; private right of action

coverage.summary: Applies to real estate lessors of residential dwelling units in Jersey City, to their agents and subcontractors, and to service providers that coordinate rent data. A residential dwelling unit is any unit intended as a person's primary residence. Inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care and detention or correctional facilities are excluded. There are no unit-count or building-age limits.
coverage.owner_conditions: The coordination definition exempts owners of multiple properties for actions related exclusively to properties controlled by the same rental property owner.
coverage.other_conditions: Licensed real estate agents are excluded from the coordination and service-provider definitions while operating in accordance with all applicable state regulations.

rules.exemptions: Owners of multiple properties, for actions related exclusively to properties controlled by the same owner. Licensed real estate agents operating in accordance with state regulations. Inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care and detention or correctional facilities are not residential dwelling units.
rules.effective_date_note: Neither Ord. 25-057 nor amending Ord. 25-076 states an effective date. Ord. 25-057 was adopted on final reading on May 21, 2025 and approved by the Mayor on May 22, 2025. Ord. 25-076 was adopted on July 16, 2025 and approved by the Mayor on July 17, 2025. A secondary law-firm alert (DX06) lists the section as "effective June 2025". The section is in force on the query date.

rules.conflict_note: Organizer open question: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect. The act was enacted July 20, 2026 and takes effect July 1, 2027, and it prohibits municipal ordinances that conflict with it. Whether § 218-12 conflicts with the act, and so would be preempted, is unresolved.
rules.review_note: The penalty for a first violation sits in Jersey City Code § 1-25, which was not captured. Both ordinances describe Chapter 218 as both "Multiple Dwellings" and "Fees and Charges". They also renumber the existing §§ 218-12 to 218-18 as §§ 218-13 to 218-19; those renumbered sections, including "Exempt dwellings" and "Conflicts with state law", are marked unchanged and their content is not shown. Ord. 25-057 refers in places to "this Act" and "this chapter". News coverage (DX11) reports that a lobbyist asked to exclude Multiple Listing Services; the ordinance text has no MLS-specific exclusion beyond the licensed-real-estate-agent carve-out. Status is inferred from adoption and mayoral approval because no effective date is stated.
rules.source_notes: The operative text is taken from Ord. 25-076 (DX04), which amends § 218-12(2). Definitions, enforcement and penalties come from base Ord. 25-057 (DX02), which Ord. 25-076 leaves unchanged. The secondary sources are consistent with the official text. DX06 (Morgan Lewis alert) gives "fines up to $2,000 per day". DX11 (Hudson County View) reports the 9-0 passage and a commenter's reference to a "$2,000 daily fine". Councilman Rivera's remark in DX11 that amendments may still happen was resolved by Ord. 25-076. Link-only D035 and D037 duplicate DX11 and DX06.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260)
rules.requirement:
Jersey City regulates residential rents through its Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260 of the Municipal Code. The Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations and the Rent Leveling Board administer and enforce it.

Landlords seeking increases beyond the ordinary limit file:
- capital improvement applications;
- vacancy capital improvement applications;
- hardship rental increase applications.

Tenants may file Illegal Rent Petitions, or Failure to Maintain Service Petitions seeking rent reductions.

All 1-4 unit properties are exempt. Owners may submit a Rent Control Exemption Request for other permitted exemptions.

The page lists a Consumer Price Index chart as a resource but does not state the cap formula or percentage.

unverifiable_exemptions: Other exemptions permitted under Chapter 260, granted on a Rent Control Exemption Request reviewed by the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations
coverage.summary: Covers rental properties with 5 or more units. All 1-4 unit properties are exempt. Other permitted exemptions are available on request.
coverage.other_conditions: Further exemptions are available if the owner meets the criteria for a permitted exemption and files a Rent Control Exemption Request.

rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties. Other permitted exemptions are available through a Rent Control Exemption Request.
rules.effective_date_note: The official city page gives no enactment or effective date for Chapter 260. The office describes the ordinance as currently administered and enforced.

Retrieve Chapter 260 to fill in the allowable increase. New Jersey has no general state rent cap, so no state rent-cap precedence question arises.
